mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: northeastern South Dakota and adjacent portions of Minnesota
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Storms could gradually evolve into an organizing cluster, with some continuing risk for severe hail and, perhaps, increasing potential to produce strong to severe wind gusts through 3-5 AM CDT.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: northeastern South Dakota and adjacent portions of Minnesota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Strong thunderstorm development has been focused within a narrow corridor east of Mobridge, aided by lift associated with low-level warm advection/frontogenesis, to the north/northeast of a weak surface low over central South Dakota. Forcing associated with a subtle short wave impulse digging within seasonably strong west-northwesterly mid/upper flow may also be providing support. As this perturbation progresses southeastward during the next few hours, the surface low is forecast to weaken with a gradual southward advancement of the near-surface frontal zone. Although storms are likely elevated above at least a shallow stable surface-based layer, they have been maintained by inflow of seasonably high moisture content supportive of large CAPE, beneath steep mid-level lapse rates associated with a plume of warm elevated mixed-layer air. This moisture, still largely concentrated over central/eastern South Dakota and Nebraska, is forecast to advect eastward in an evolving plume along the frontal zone across southern Minnesota/northern Iowa through 9-11Z. As it does, as least some convection allowing-guidance suggests potential for continuing upscale growth into an organizing cluster, which may eventually pose increasing potential to produce strong to severe surface gusts.
